history.period: Lingam moved from Kushasthali in 1560; present structure built ~1740s under Marathas (Mangeshi village donated by Peshwas in 1739), rebuilt 1890; jiroddhara concluded 17 February 1973
history.summary: CSV town CORRECTED: the temple is NOT in Panaji — it is at Mangeshi village, Priol, Ponda taluka, 21–22 km from Panaji. The Manguesh linga originated at Kushasthali (Cortalim), Salcete; after the Portuguese took Salcete in 1543 and began conversions in 1560, Saraswat Brahmins of the Vatsa (and Kaundinya) gotra moved the linga to Mangeshi in Antruz Mahal (Ponda), then ruled by the Hindu kings of Sonde, to keep it secure — temple records date the move to Shaka 1482 (1560 CE), and Jesuit reports confirm it happened before 1 May 1560. The original Priol structure was simple; the present building was erected under Maratha rule about 150 years later — the Peshwas donated Mangeshi village to the temple in 1739 at the instance of Sardar Ramchandra Malhar Sukhtankar — with further building in 1890 and a final jiroddhara on 17 February 1973, when a golden kalasha was fitted atop the tallest dome. The complex has a seven-storey deepastambha, a prominent Nandi, a water tank believed to be its oldest part, a sabha mandapa, agrashalas and a wooden rath; it is among Goa's largest and most-visited temples. Shrimad Swamiji of Shri Kavale Math is the spiritual head. NOTE: the temple's Wikipedia infobox still lists 'South Goa' district, but Ponda taluka has been in North Goa district since the 2015 bifurcation; coordinates from OpenStreetMap (15.44489, 73.96645) are corroborated by a tour operator at 15.44490, 73.96656.

name: Shri Mangeshi Temple
town_description: Mangeshi is a village in Ponda taluka of North Goa, about 21–22 km from Panaji near Mardol and Nagueshi, famous for the Shri Manguesh temple; Lata Mangeshkar's father Deenanath was born in this village.

travel.airport: Dabolim (Goa International) Airport about 30 km; Manohar International Airport (Mopa) about 35 km.
travel.railway: Karmali station about 8 km; Thivim about 25 km.
travel.road: About 21–22 km from Panaji on Dinanath Mangeshkar Road; 1 km from Mardol; reachable by bus and taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri and the Magha Poornima Jatrotsav draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily (single tour-operator source — verify). Dress code applies: shorts or inappropriate attire not allowed inside the temple (instituted 2011).
